_note: Pairing and spacing tips shown with food suggestions (WHO, ICMR-NIN Dietary Guidelines for Indians 2024).

iron.text: Have it with something sour: lemon, amla, guava or tomato help your body take up the iron.
Keep tea and coffee an hour away from meals; they block iron.
Have curd and milk at a different meal from your iron-rich food.
Cooking sabzi or dal in an iron kadai adds a little iron.
Sprouting and fermenting (sprouts, idli, dosa) make iron easier to absorb.
Double-fortified salt and fortified rice from the ration shop add iron at no extra cost.

b12.text: Curd, milk and paneer each day add B12; with no dairy or eggs, food alone is often not enough.

vitd.text: 15–20 minutes of mid-morning sun on your arms and face, most days.

sugar.text: Fill half your plate with dal and vegetables first, then rice or roti.
A 10-minute walk after your biggest meal.

bp.text: Less salt: pickles, papad, namkeen and packaged snacks hold the most.
Fruit and greens each day add potassium, which helps BP.

lipids.text: Measure cooking oil (about 4 teaspoons a day) and keep fried snacks to once a week.
